summary: A worker can hand in last year's form while the agency finishes replacing it.
realLife: In January 2018 the IRS temporarily allowed employees to keep using the 2017 W-4 through March 30 while the revised form was being introduced. IRS drew a different distinction in 2020. An ordinary W-4 already on file could continue to govern pay, while a worker changing an election had to use the redesigned form.
inGame: needs: a transition notice gives the prior form a specific end date.
gates: A transition notice gives the prior form a specific end date.

turns.pulledBy: The form arrives inside the window.
turns.writesBack: The employee keeps the dated receipt.

turns.pulledBy: It arrives after the window closes.
turns.writesBack: The employee gets a second paperwork task.

turns.what: Payroll keeps the existing election when the redesigned form arrives.
turns.pulledBy: In a later payroll review, the same employee still has an ordinary pre-2020 election on file and requests no change.
turns.writesBack: The payroll record retains the original filing date without flagging the employee for a missing form.
